basis: CIF NWE / Dated Brent physical proxy
note: Brent briefly topped $100 before easing to about $99.55 (WTI near $91), heading for a ~13% weekly gain, as the crisis widens beyond the Gulf: Kazakhstan's main export route — the CPC terminal on Russia's Black Sea coast — suspended loadings after vessel attacks, cutting Tengiz output roughly 925k→406k b/d, while Hormuz traffic hit its lowest since 7 May (one oil tanker Thursday) and Saudi Arabia began shifting cargoes to Egypt's Mediterranean coast at Sidi Kerir. Bab el-Mandeb is still functioning (~32 tanker crossings, nine crude) but routing is lengthening. Physical NWE differentials remain firm; European low-sulphur gasoil near a record ~$60/bbl premium over Brent. Editorial proxy, not a traded quote — indicative, and watch tanker-transit data over the rhetoric.
